customer-service: Every reply answers the customer's actual question in the first two sentences.
Refunds, cancellations and account changes follow the written policy; anything outside it is escalated, not improvised.
Tickets are tagged with category and priority (P1-P4) before they are answered.
No customer data, order numbers or emails are pasted into third-party tools that are not approved.
Sending a reply, closing a ticket or issuing a refund through an MCP server happens only after the owner approved that tool.
Knowledge-base articles cite the ticket pattern they came from and are reviewed before publishing.
Escalations include a one-paragraph summary, what was tried, and what the customer was told.
marketing: Every claim in the copy can be traced to a source the owner gave you or a public page you link.
Campaigns name one audience, one offer and one primary metric before any copy is written.
SEO work starts from real search data or a stated assumption, never invented volumes.
Nothing is published, posted, emailed or spent (ads budget) without the owner's explicit approval.
Brand voice: read the brand guide or brand-voice skill first; flag anything that conflicts with it.
Reports show numbers with their source and date; no fake-precise figures.
Remove AI-writing tells (filler intros, em-dash chains, generic superlatives) before handing off.
design: One visual direction was picked from UI Hub, with 2-4 named reference previews and the reasons; rejected clusters are written down.
A token sheet exists (4-6 colours with hex, type roles, radius scale, one card padding) before any CSS.
Long links, repo paths and commands wrap (overflow-wrap:anywhere) and never overflow a card.
All cards of a kind share the same padding and align their actions.
Text and controls pass WCAG 2.2 AA contrast in light and dark; keyboard focus is visible.
Motion uses transform/opacity only, has one orchestrated moment per page, and honours prefers-reduced-motion.
Four screenshots were checked: desktop 1440 and mobile 390, each in light and dark.
Lighthouse (or an equivalent audit) was run and every accessibility issue fixed.

goals.customer-service: Learn to triage, answer and escalate customer requests with written policies, a help-desk MCP if allowed, and a self-check before sending.
goals.marketing: Learn to plan, write and measure marketing work (content, SEO, email, ads) from real skills and prompts, without publishing anything unapproved.
goals.design: Learn to design an interface that does not look templated: pick one style from UI Hub, follow design skills, build, and verify with four screenshots.

permissions.customer-service: Read-only by default. Help-desk MCP servers (Zendesk, Freshdesk, Intercom, ...) need API keys and can send replies; ask the owner first.
permissions.marketing: Read-only by default. Email, ads and social MCP servers need credentials and can publish or spend money; ask the owner first.
permissions.design: Mostly read-only. Figma/Canva MCP servers need tokens; skills are text you can read. Installing a skill writes files into the project; ask first.
